packet.description_seed: Mammalian meat allergy is a growing problem along Australia's east coast - and it's caused by tick bites.

clean_source_blocks.text: Mammalian meat allergy is a growing problem along Australia's east coast - and it's caused by tick bites.

​​Just over a year later, in June 2022, Jeremy died after eating a beef sausage on a camping trip with friends at a beach north of Sydney. The cause of death was initially recorded simply as asthma. But in February, after an inquest pushed for by his family, a coroner ruled that the asthma attack and resulting fatal anaphylaxis was triggered by tick-induced mammalian meat allergy (MMA). His death is the first in the world known to have been caused by MMA, also known as alpha-gal syndrome. Diagnosed cases of MMA have steadily escalated since 2007, when an Australian doctor first discovered the allergy was linked to tick bites. Now, scientists and campaigners are warning that the condition, though easily prevented, can be unexpectedly triggered - and could pose a deadly threat.

Tick bites are driving up deadly meat allergies. Scientists are scrambling to stop it Alpha-gal syndrome is increasing across the U.S., driven by lone star ticks By Mary Randolph edited by Claire Cameron Tick season is booming, and with it come fears over a potentially deadly tick-borne allergy to meat. Discovered just under 20 years ago, alpha-gal syndrome is caused by bites from the lone star tick in the U.S., though other ticks can trigger the illness in other parts of the world. At least one person is known to have died because of the disease, but scientists know relatively little about it—including how to best treat it. Now researchers have met for the first-ever scientific conference dedicated to alpha-gal to try to tease out some answers.

Jeremy Webb died of anaphylaxis triggered by tick-induced mammalian meat allergy When Myfanwy Webb looks back at her birthday party five years ago, she is overcome with regret - remembering what she now sees as a missed opportunity to save her son's life. Hours after a celebratory lunch at a restaurant Jeremy began having difficulty breathing. His parents called an ambulance, and the then-15-year-old began vomiting. At the hospital, doctors noted that Jeremy had a suspected meat allergy, but ultimately blamed the episode on his asthma, which he'd had since he was a toddler. He was sent home the next day. "I made the wrong decision," Webb says, wishing she had asked for more testing. If she had, doctors might have established that Jeremy had actually been suffering from anaphylaxis, and sent him home with an EpiPen.

payload.title: Puutiaisen purema voi laukaista hengenvaarallisen liha-allergian
payload.summary: Puutiaisen purema voi laukaista alfa-gal-oireyhtymän ja hengenvaarallisen anafylaksian. Jeremy Webbin kuolema on vahvistettu ensimmäiseksi tunnetuksi oireyhtymän aiheuttamaksi kuolemantapaukseksi.
payload.content:
[BBC:n](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cj6g03567edo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss) mukaan puutiaisen pureman laukaisema nisäkkäiden lihaan liittyvä allergia eli alfa-gal-oireyhtymä on kasvava ongelma Australian itärannikolla. Oireyhtymä voi aiheuttaa hengenvaarallisen anafylaksian. Australiassa Jeremy Webbin kuolema on vahvistettu ensimmäiseksi tunnetuksi tapaukseksi maailmassa, jossa puutiaisen puremaan liittyvä liha-allergia johti kuolemaan. Tapauksen tutkinta muutti alun perin astmaksi kirjatun kuolemansyyn.

## Oireet tulkittiin astmaksi

Webb sai vakavan allergisen reaktion 15-vuotiaana äitinsä Myfanwy Webbin syntymäpäivälounaan jälkeen. Hengitysvaikeudet ja oksentelu alkoivat tunteja ravintola-aterian jälkeen, joten hänen vanhempansa kutsuivat ambulanssin. Sairaalassa lääkärit kirjasivat epäilyn liha-allergiasta, mutta päättelivät oireiden johtuneen astmasta, jota hän oli sairastanut taaperoiästä lähtien. Webb lähetettiin kotiin seuraavana päivänä.

Myfanwy Webb on jälkeenpäin pitänyt tapahtunutta menetettynä mahdollisuutena pelastaa poikansa. Hän sanoo katuvansa, ettei pyytänyt Jeremylle lisätutkimuksia. Tutkimuksissa olisi voitu todeta, että kyse oli astman sijasta anafylaksiasta, ja Jeremy olisi voitu lähettää kotiin vakavan allergisen reaktion hoitoon tarkoitetun adrenaliinikynän kanssa.

## Kuolemansyy varmistui vasta tutkinnassa

Hieman yli vuotta sairaalakäynnin jälkeen, kesäkuussa 2022, Jeremy kuoli syötyään naudanlihamakkaran ystäviensä kanssa leiriretkellä rannalla Sydneyn pohjoispuolella. Kuolemansyyksi kirjattiin aluksi pelkästään astma. Perheen ajaman tutkinnan jälkeen kuolemansyyn tutkija katsoi helmikuussa, että astmakohtauksen ja sitä seuranneen kuolemaan johtaneen anafylaksian laukaisi puutiaisen pureman aiheuttama nisäkkäiden liha-allergia.

## Diagnoosit lisääntyvät

Australialainen lääkäri havaitsi vuonna 2007, että allergia liittyy puutiaisten puremiin. Diagnosoitujen tapausten määrä on sen jälkeen kasvanut tasaisesti. Yhdysvalloissa alfa-gal-oireyhtymä on yleistynyt, ja erityisesti lone star -puutiaisen puremat ovat sairauden taustalla, [Scientific American kertoo](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/deadly-meat-allergies-from-tick-bites-are-on-the-rise-should-you-be-worried/). Lehden mukaan myös muut puutiaislajit voivat muualla maailmassa laukaista oireyhtymän.

[Scientific Americanin](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/deadly-meat-allergies-from-tick-bites-are-on-the-rise-should-you-be-worried/) mukaan tutkijat tuntevat oireyhtymää vielä puutteellisesti, eikä parhaasta hoidosta ole varmuutta. Lehti kertoo, että ensimmäinen pelkästään alfa-gal-oireyhtymään keskittynyt tieteellinen konferenssi kokosi tutkijoita etsimään vastauksia esimerkiksi hoitoa koskeviin avoimiin kysymyksiin. BBC:n mukaan tutkijat ja kampanjoijat varoittavat, että sairaus voi laueta odottamatta ja muodostaa hengenvaarallisen uhan.
summary_bullets: Puutiaisen purema voi laukaista nisäkkäiden lihaan liittyvän alfa-gal-oireyhtymän.
Jeremy Webbin kuolema on ensimmäinen tunnettu oireyhtymän aiheuttama kuolemantapaus.
Webbin kuolemansyy kirjattiin ensin astmaksi ja korjattiin tutkinnan jälkeen.
payload.journalist_note: Aihe käsittelee Australiaa ja Yhdysvaltoja, joten paketin Kotimaa-luokitus korjattiin Ulkomaat-luokaksi.

BBC:n mukaan tutkijat ja kampanjoijat varoittavat, että sairaus voi laueta odottamatta ja muodostaa hengenvaarallisen uhan.

Mammalian meat allergy is a growing problem along Australia's east coast - and it's caused by tick bites.

​​Just over a year later, in June 2022, Jeremy died after eating a beef sausage on a camping trip with friends at a beach north of Sydney. The cause of death was initially recorded simply as asthma. But in February, after an inquest pushed for by his family, a coroner ruled that the asthma attack and resulting fatal anaphylaxis was triggered by tick-induced mammalian meat allergy (MMA). His death is the first in the world known to have been caused by MMA, also known as alpha-gal syndrome. Diagnosed cases of MMA have steadily escalated since 2007, when an Australian doctor first discovered the allergy was linked to tick bites. Now, scientists and campaigners are warning that the condition, though easily prevented, can be unexpectedly triggered - and could pose a deadly threat.

Tick bites are driving up deadly meat allergies. Scientists are scrambling to stop it Alpha-gal syndrome is increasing across the U.S., driven by lone star ticks By Mary Randolph edited by Claire Cameron Tick season is booming, and with it come fears over a potentially deadly tick-borne allergy to meat. Discovered just under 20 years ago, alpha-gal syndrome is caused by bites from the lone star tick in the U.S., though other ticks can trigger the illness in other parts of the world. At least one person is known to have died because of the disease, but scientists know relatively little about it—including how to best treat it. Now researchers have met for the first-ever scientific conference dedicated to alpha-gal to try to tease out some answers.

Jeremy Webb died of anaphylaxis triggered by tick-induced mammalian meat allergy When Myfanwy Webb looks back at her birthday party five years ago, she is overcome with regret - remembering what she now sees as a missed opportunity to save her son's life. Hours after a celebratory lunch at a restaurant Jeremy began having difficulty breathing. His parents called an ambulance, and the then-15-year-old began vomiting. At the hospital, doctors noted that Jeremy had a suspected meat allergy, but ultimately blamed the episode on his asthma, which he'd had since he was a toddler. He was sent home the next day. "I made the wrong decision," Webb says, wishing she had asked for more testing. If she had, doctors might have established that Jeremy had actually been suffering from anaphylaxis, and sent him home with an EpiPen.
